the temperature dependence of unthermalization nonequilibrium charge-carrier mobility in cubic Zn S is nonlinear at low temperatures, and linear at high temperatures.

the temperature dependence of the mobility of nonthermalized carriers.
the temperature dependence of the mobility of nonthermalized non-equilibrium charge carriers in a semiconductor.
the temperature dependence of the nonequilibrium charge-carrier mobility in cubic Zn S crystals.

in the case of the cubic ZnS, the mobility of nonthermalized charge carriers at temperatures far from phase transitions is a nonlinear function of temperature, which is independent of the ratio between scattering mechanisms.
the mobility of charge carriers in ZnS is a function of temperature, which is not only nonlinear but also depends on the scattering mechanism.
the temperature dependence of mobility is determined not only by scattering mechanisms but also by the temperature dependence of the energy of nonthermally nonequilibrium charge carries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mobility is a function of both the temperature and the energy of non-thermalized nonequilibirum charge carriers.
the mobility of nonthermalized carriers in cubic ZnS is independent of temperature.
the mobility of nonthermalized carriers in cubic ZnS at room temperature is determined by the interaction of the carriers with acoustic and optical phonons and is independent of temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mobility is temperature independent in the region where the scattering of nonequilibrium charge carries is mainly caused by the acoustic phonons, and the temperature dependence of the mobility in the other region is determined by the ratio between the acoustic and optical phonon contributions.

the mobility of nonthermalized non-equilibrium charge carriers can be independent of temperature, which is a very important result for the theory of the transport properties of solids and the development of new materials for electronic devices and optoelectronic devices.
